notes.title: Update notes: 2022-03-06
notes.notes:
Due to popular demand of having the end game be less grindy I've changed the biomass amplifier as follows:


 greatly decreased upgrade cost (max. level is now 20T, down from 45T)
 increased the amplifier's output boost by 20% per level (was 10%)


I hope this makes things a bit easier for y'all! Enjoy!

notes.title: Hotfix: The Woman in the High Castle achievement
notes.notes:
I got reports that the Woman in the High Castle achievement didn't seem to track properly. After investigating the issue I found out that while the tracking was working fine the achievement on the Steam backend used a different value than it had in-game (500k in-game, 1 million on Steam). 

This issue has now been resolved. A client patch is not needed.

notes.title: Hotfix: Upgrade button for Biomass Amplifier
notes.notes: Last hotfix I already attempted to fix the upgrade button for the Biomass Amplifier appearing too early but it had the opposite effect as now it didn't appear at all. This update should finally fix this once and for all. Apologies for any inconvenience caused.

notes.title: 1.0 Hotfix
notes.notes: This update fixes a bug causing the Magic Biomass Amplifier to become upgradeable before hitting 50% castle donations.

notes.title: v1.0 Release - Leaving Early Access
notes.notes:
We're leaving Early Access today!

One thing however needed to be addressed - the donation values of several items were just too low so I've rebalanced them all. Should go much quicker now!

notes.title: 0.9 EA Hotfix 1
notes.notes:
A hotfix has been deployed fixing the following issues:


fixed an issue causing the Lumberjack's campfire to ignore the SFX volume slider
fixed an issue causing some of the Queen's dialogue to appear every time the player started the game
fixed a serious issue causing an exception when talents were reset which subsequently led to no Gemstones being refunded
reimplemented Steam stat tracking. Before, stats were sent to Steam whenever they changed, which was a bad idea because Steam doesn't like that. Now, they only get sent on game start and then every 120 seconds after that. This should make stat tracking much more reliable. If the player quits the game before the stats are uploaded they get cached and uploaded on the next game start.

A note on the update size: with the last build I made the mistake to have Unity use the maximum available compression. While this caused the game to become much smaller on disk it also meant the Steam download would be the entire game on every update. This wasn't what I intended to happen so the change has been reverted. This however means you'll have to download the entire game again but only this once. I apologize for any issues this may have caused.

notes.title: Version 0.9 EA - The Woman in the High Castle
notes.notes:
Took me a while - had other things to do - but here it finally is: the last content update!

"The Woman in the High Castle" brings a new end-game threat: a flying castle positioned over your precious village. The castle's ruler? A not so friendly queen, and she's got demands because of course she has.

The flying castle part is unlocked after upgrading the Statue to the maximum level.

I've also done much more with the dialogue (well, more "monologue") system. It now supports different characters, even within a dialogue, and there's much more dialogue in general. I've also added a small cast of new colorful characters which all take part in the new end-game.

This is the final version before the game leaves Early Access and is considered "complete". This build is pretty much the final beta - I'll see if there are any issues cropping up and if not the final version will be released.

If you encounter any issues, please report them on Discord - https://discord.gg/whJpBh6h

notes.title: Update notes for 2021-12-18
notes.notes:
Kingdom of Assetia - The Clicker Game will be part of the Steam Holiday Sale where it'll be offered with a 25% discount. 

Here's a small update to bring the holiday season into the world of Assetia as well. I'm not much of a decorator (not even my home is decorated, much to the dismay of my wife) so it's a little bare-bones but hey, it's not nothing!

Events

snow will appear in-game starting December 1 (so it's already there now) and melt at the end of February
holiday decorations will appear starting December 23 and last until December 27
added some holiday decorations
added some more winter decorations


Bug Fixes

notes.title: Hotfix: fix breaking savegames
notes.notes:
Seems like the last update did indeed break something as everyone who launched the game after the update had their progress wiped. Ahhh!

This hotfix, well, fixes the issue.

notes.title: Sign of life, plus a minor update
notes.notes:
Dear players,

you might have wondered where I have gone or if the game is dead in the water as so many EA games are. This is all my fault. I got hooked on Amazon Games' "New World" and well ... suddenly it's more than two months later and I haven't worked on Assetia at all :( 

I can only apologize to you, but that's how I work. I am a single developer and do this as a hobby. At some point I tend to lose track and need to recharge my creative batteries by doing something else instead - in this case, get hooked on a terrible yet oddly addicting MMORPG. However it's not like I entirely forgot what I was doing - I do still have a content update mapped out and at least some groundwork has been laid already. What I do not have, however, is a release date, not even an estimate. It's done when it's done.

Because I didn't want to just post a sign of life I've also included a tiny update to the game which improves things a little bit for new players. Most of them wondered how to open the production menu on the Baker, Blacksmith or Tavern, because right-clicking feels so damn unintuitive in a clicker game. For that reason the building's tooltips now include a hint pointing players in the right direction. I still think this is rather unintuitive but for now it's the best I can do without messing up the UI too much (yes, a button would be an option ... but I don't like it for aesthetic reasons).

I hope you aren't too mad at me for going radio silent for so long. I'm still here!

notes.title: Hotfix: prevent crash when screen resolution list changes
notes.notes:
If the list of available screen resolutions changed for any reason a bug could cause a crash in the studio splash screen. This only happened in three scenarios:


 multi-monitor setup with one screen switched off when it was on before
 new monitor
 new graphics card

This hotfix prevents the crash and applies the default resolution instead if the selected resolution is no longer available.

notes.title: Hotfix: now supporting aspect rations other than 16:9
notes.notes:

Note that the update may cause your selected resolution to reset anyway. You can set it again in the options menu.

notes.title: EA Version 0.3: The Mysterious Crystal awakens!
notes.notes:
Early Access Version 0.3 is here!

Production

The Mysterious Crystal has awakened and grants production boosts - but only if appeased using Gemstones. These equally mysterious stones can be obtained as a rare drop from any Iron related activity (mining and smelting Iron Ore). The longer a recipe takes to complete the more likely is it to obtain a Gemstone.

Gemstones already started to drop in an earlier update so you might have already gotten some. If you did the Mysterious Crystal will sport a typical yellow outline.

Selected boosts can be reset at any time with a full refund of all Gemstones spent.

Bugfixes

fixed a pathing issue for carriers on the Storage to Farm/Distillery route causing them to get stuck on carriers coming from the opposite direction


What's next?

Next on the agenda is adding sound effects and music as well as adding volume sliders to the Options menu.

notes.title: Everything changes ... again. Plus something new!
notes.notes:
I must admit that after the value overflow crash desaster I was disheartened. I couldn't see a proper way to fix it. While I did release an update that prevented the crash from happening it also was pretty damn terrible in terms of game balance.

So I worked over the last few days to remedy the situation and to be able to move forward without hopefully ever having to touch base systems again. This update is the result.

To the players who stuck with this from day one: balance has changed entirely. Like, totally. This means the money you have on your savegames might be enough to upgrade all 5 buildings to the maximum level. I actually don't know if thats possible - I am sure you'll tell me soon enough - but if it is I'm really sorry. Doing this was the only way I could fix the game for old and new players.

The game is still in Early Access for exactly that reason: getting the balance right. I just hope this was the last time

Balance Changes

every building and upgrade has been rebalanced and progression is now way more natural
tick length is back up to 2 seconds and cannot be reduced
generated money is way down, but so are upgrade costs
however, each building has a "second upgrade stage" that starts at half the building's max level. At that point, upgrading it will become way more expensive.
production buildings now unlock at level 40 (Baker - unlocks the farm/mill/chicken part) and 50 (Blacksmith, unlocks the mine)
upgrading using Magic Stones now starts at the mentioned "second upgrade stage". For example, for the house that's level 50, and for the statue level 250.


Production

To finally be able to smelt Iron Ore a new dwarven forge has been discovered and it just so happens it's right next to the mine. Who'd have known? You can sell Iron Bars directly to the Blacksmith for Magic Stones. Obviously there's an achievement for producing Iron Bars and also there's one for obtaining 500 Magic Stone now.

Bug Fixes

It's no longer possible to upgrade a building past the maximum level by batch upgrading. No idea how I missed this!

Misc

You can now reset your game progress via the options menu. Be aware this rewinds the save game to zero and cannot be undone. Yes, there's a security check before, no worries!

notes.title: Hotfix for crash bug, please read for details!
notes.notes:
Today's update is a little different and does not include any new content.

A show stopping crash bug has been discovered yesterday which is related to how the money values are stored. Fixing this required an almost complete overhaul of anything related to money. 

While this is good news - fixing severe bugs early is better than running into them late - it means that some things have changed:


all values related to money are now absolutely infinite. This means these kind of bugs can't occur ever again.
previous savegames work - mostly. Everything except money can be restored. Yes, this means your money will reset to zero, but at least with my savegame this didn't cause any problems as the income was high enough to instantly fill the coffers again.
any upgrade that increased the tick rate now increases money by a percentage instead
to compensate, the tick rate is now always 1 second
as the game no longer uses floating point numbers, everything had to be rebalanced. Not sure how that worked out so another balance pass might be needed.


I apologize for the inconvenience, but I just can't keep a severe bug like this in the game. I was ready to band-aid it yesterday but after thinking it over I decided to go the better, yet inconvenient, route.

Known Bugs

Some achievement's progress bars are invisible right now. The bug is already fixed but the fix didn't make it in the current build.

notes.title: New production buildings, bugfixes & more!
notes.notes:
This is hardly a "small update" but Steam always wants me to upload a new picture for bigger ones which I don't want to do. 

There's a lot going on in this version. New production buildings have been added, additional recipes are available for longer-term production and some annoying bugs have been fixed.

Of course, there are new achievements to obtain as well. 

Production

you can now have the new Chicken Coop produce Eggs which are used by the Bakery to produce Cookies to sell on the Market
you can also use Wheat to produce Moonshine in the Distillery which can then be sold directly via the Tavern
a new iron mine has opened! It unlocks at Blacksmith level 55 and produces - who'd have known? - Iron Ore. There's currently no need for Iron Ore anywhere, but there will be soon so start producing!
added a recipe to produce 10 Wheat in one go at the time cost of producing 11. Hey, the farmer needs her sleep too!
added a recipe to mill 5 Wheat at once at the time cost of producing 5.5 - after that, the miller's apprentice has to clean the mill stone!
added a recipe to produce 5 Eggs at the time cost of producing 6. Poor hens.
added a recipe to make 4 Moonshine in 9 Hours. Because who makes moonshine for just 2 hours a night?


Balancing

slightly buffed the Statue's late game income production


Misc Features

UI windows now open at a position relative to the screen height
added a resolution selection to the Options menu
moved unused UI windows way below 4K resolution so they don't accidentally show on screen even when not active
the "Switch to Village" button now also lights up when production on the village screen is completed (like the Tavern, Market etc.)
internal groundwork has been laid for timed ingame events (nothing visible yet!)
you can now switch between village and production screens using left/right arrow keys or A/D keys


Bugfixes

fixed a bug preventing the inventory from being properly loaded from the save game after new achievements have been added to the game
the "Switch to Production" button no longer lights up when the production building in question is already on the screen
hopefully fixed the missing Blacksmith upgrade button on some resolutions
prevented clicks on the user interface affecting objects behind it ("clickthrough effect")

Thanks for reporting these issues!

notes.title: Early Access Version 0.2
notes.notes:
11.09.2021 - EA 0.2

This is the first major update!

New Systems

The first alternate advancement system is in! After reaching level 30 on the Bakery you can now access a second environment where you can farm wheat, mill it to flour and then have the bakery produce bread to sell on the new market stall. However, selling goods doesn't earn money. Instead, you'll get a Magic Stone you can use to upgrade any passive building (House, Bakery, Blacksmith, Tavern and Statue) that has already reached level 50 by one level for free. Production processes also run while you
aren't playing so check back regularly!

Important: to access the Bakery's production menu, please use the right mouse button. On all other production buildings the menu opens on the left mouse button. This is because the Bakery also produces money on left-click.

For the achievement hunters among you of course there are new achievements linked to the production chain as well.

This is only the beginning. There will be much more production chains in the future, including themed ones on certain holidays!

Also, please ignore the rather bleak landscape - it's not done yet.

Balancing Changes

some more tuning was done on all buildings
greatly increased the multipliers on all percentage-based upgrades

Bugfixes

fixed a display bug on the Tavern and the Statue suggesting way lower income than they actually provided
fixed the last few instances of floats being used instead of doubles
fixed the Steam name for the You Shall not Pass! achievement
fixed the Statue achievement not becoming available despite the Statue being unlocked
fixed a race condition preventing achievement stats from being restored

Misc Changes

multiple upgrades can now be applied at once by holding shift while clicking the button
added achievements for the Statue's Plaza and Benches
added a graphics quality option to the options menu
added abbreviations for numbers ranging from Nonillion to Unvigintillion
number abbreviations are now colored in a different color than the actual number to prevent confusing "o" (Octillion) with "0" (zero)
you can now change graphics quality in the Options window

Known Bugs

the production menu puts recipes in the vertical center, not the top of the scrollable area. This will be fixed in a later update.
items do not yet have tooltips


As usual, please report any and all bugs you might find (and I'm sure there are some I never even noticed) on the forums so I may squash them swiftly and without mercy!

notes.title: Second balancing pass update and more!
notes.notes:
In yesterday's attempt at balancing the game I messed up the values even more - now upgrading was more expensive. You rightfully complained about it so here's an update to address this.

Balancing Changes

updated values for the first two buildings - House and Bakery - to make progression a lot easier until about level 20
level requirements to unlock the Bakery and Blacksmith have been drastically reduced
upgrades now also make much more sense, especially the Quest Giver who now increases total income by 5% (was 1%) per level
income Steam achievement requirements have been changed to require billions, not millions. Not that this changes much as you can earn billions rather easily now.

Bug fixes

fixed a bug preventing the income % increase to work properly
upgrades providing an income now use humanized numbers

Features

upgrade buttons ready to upgrade now have a shiny effect so they are easier to spot
the game window can now be resized in windowed mode

Naturally, where there's light there's shadow. Currently known bugs are:

upgrading the Blacksmith doesn't color the house
tutorial dialogue might happen at inappropiate times which is related to the balancing changes

I hope this update fixes the game at least to a degree where it becomes more playable. I will work on balance changes for the remaining buildings tomorrow so stay tuned!

notes.title: First balance pass update
notes.notes:
I have just released the first balancing update, making severe changes to all values across the board.

The main problem was that while upgrade costs were increased exponentially, income was not. This update fixes this. Each building now has an exponent value to increase income by, depending on its place in the progression. Building base upgrade costs were also increased to be more in line with the new income values. 

Some upgrades have also seen changes, especially those with flat income (now also increasing exponentially) and those who reduce tick time (these now reduce tick time more).

Of course, now the money earned achievements make little sense so they'll have to be changed as well, but before I do that I'd like to get feedback on this balancing pass. I assume there'll still be something to even out, so please don't hesitate to tell me.
